title: A Javanese gamelan at the 1889 Paris fair inspired Debussy
body: At the 1889 World’s Fair in Paris, the young Claude Debussy heard a Javanese gamelan, an ensemble built mainly from tuned bronze gongs and metallophones. Its layered, cycling patterns and tunings that don’t match Western scales made a deep impression. Echoes appear in later pieces such as Pagodes from 1903, and gamelan has since influenced composers from John Cage to Benjamin Britten.
